instruction: Include the specified web article reference in the References section.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

rules.citation_text: Williams, K. (2021, March 15). The impact of e-commerce on retail markets. Business Today Online. Retrieved from https://www.businesstoday.com/articles/ecommerce-impact

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding an online article reference citation to the References section of the essay. The evaluator checks if the complete online article citation appears in the document after the agent completes the task. The custom getter extracts all text from the document, and the metric function checks if the expected citation text is present.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts only References section text (docx_reference.py:39-59): searches for References heading (line 43), sets flag when found (line 44), collects only text when in_references_section=True (lines 49-57), stops at next section (lines 52-54).

Metric properly validates References section presence (docx_reference.py:24-26): checks for references/bibliography/works cited headings before verifying citation, preventing false positives from citations in essay body.

Complete coverage of instruction requirements: (a) citation text must be present - verified by lines 33-34; (b) must be in References section - verified by lines 24-26 and getter's section-specific extraction.
Correct parameter handling: metric uses expected.get('citation_text') for type='rule' (line 16), properly accessing rules dict directly.
Whitespace normalization (lines 29-30) ensures robust comparison despite formatting variations.
Postconfig appropriately saves document with Ctrl+S before reading (lines 31-54), ensuring file state is fresh.
Minor edge case: section boundary detection uses heuristic (short uppercase text) which may not catch all section headings, but this is reasonable for most documents.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider enhancing section boundary detection to handle more edge cases (e.g., numbered sections like '5. Conclusion', styled headings).
Could add explicit check for common non-References headings (Conclusion, Appendix, etc.) to improve section boundary detection robustness.
